decisions.reason: The client states that without a referral code both the ticket and its associated commission are assigned randomly, necessarily replacing the commission's weighted-draw recipient selection. The conflicting commission amounts remain unresolved and are not updated.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, 34 mints should correspond to 34 tickets and 34 x $20 commissions.

A mint still produces a ticket and commission even when no referral code is supplied.

Accounting works correctly on the leaderboards and NFT attributes whenever a code is used. That part is perfect.

Without a referral code, the ticket and commission are assigned randomly, but both must still appear on the leaderboard and in the NFT attributes.

Since your latest fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 7 mints seem to have been recorded correctly, which is great. The earlier missing tickets have not been backfilled, though.

The $18 commissions generated by these no-code buys are also still missing from the leaderboard and NFT attributes.

My screenshot shows an NFT with 9 tickets but only 4 x $20 commissions. That should be impossible because every ticket comes with a $18 commission.

The leaderboard screenshot accounts for only 15 tickets and 12 x $8 commissions from 34 total mints. Regardless of whether a referral code was supplied, 34 mints should produce 34 tickets and 34 x $20 commissions.

value_updates.recipient_selection: owner of the randomly selected eligible NFT

decisions.reason: The source changes no-referral allocation. Coded-referral ticket issuance remains one ticket to the NFT associated with the supplied code and is separately reported as working.

The source Requirement change concerns ticket allocation when no code is supplied. The coded-referral commission already has a same-message amount update and its trigger, recipient, and payout behavior remain unchanged.
The existing FAQ statements that successful referrals generate tickets remain valid; the source does not instruct a FAQ revision or provide unambiguous replacement commission copy.
Changing rewards for a mint with no referral code does not alter which supplied referral identifiers are valid or the prohibition on self-referrals.
Random allocation of a no-code mint's ticket does not change an NFT's permanent token-serial referral identity or its display locations.
The no-referral ticket issuance change does not alter the Small Block winner count, prize amount, draw trigger, pool funding, or ticket-weighted winner eligibility.
The source changes how a new no-referral ticket is allocated, not how active tickets or other NFT-linked properties behave after transfer.
Changing the number and initial recipient of a no-referral ticket does not change Small Block ticket eligibility, expiration, burning, reset, or carry-forward behavior.
The landing-page statements that each referral adds an entry remain valid and do not assert that no-code mints receive no ticket. The source does not request a landing-page copy change.

The source does not change the About page's recorded structure or topic inventory, and it does not resolve the page's separate prize-payout ambiguity or supply unambiguous replacement commission copy.
The source says the no-code recipient is selected randomly but does not require Chainlink VRF for that allocation. The existing VRF requirement for the Small Block draw remains unchanged.
